results.title: Godfred Seidu Jasaw proposes mandatory procurement of prison-made goods by government institutions
results.content: The Chairman of Parliament’s Food, Agriculture and Cocoa Affairs Committee and member of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), Dr Godfred Seidu Jasaw, has called for a government directive requiring public institutions to purchase a quota of goods produced by inmates of the Ghana Prisons Service. He said the policy would provide a reliable market for prison-based vocational businesses and help the Service generate sustainable income instead of relying heavily on philanthropy and donor support. Dr Jasaw made the proposal during an engagement between the PAC and the Ghana Prisons Service on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, following concerns raised by the Service’s Director-General, Patience Baffoe-Bonnie, about inadequate funding and limited support for its vocational enterprises.

results.title: Delayed HIV test results, misconceptions fuel concerns over stigma in Ghana
results.content: Delays in receiving HIV test results and persistent misconceptions about how the virus spreads are raising concerns about Ghana’s efforts to improve HIV services and tackle stigma against people living with the virus. The concerns emerged at the launch of the Community-Led Monitoring (CLM) initiative for HIV, tuberculosis and malaria services, organised by AngloGold Ashanti (AGAMAL). AGAMAL’s Head of Programmes, Malik Kofi Assan, said the initiative would help identify gaps in healthcare delivery and strengthen accountability in services for the three diseases.

results.title: FDA shuts down Arcan Bitters factory again over illegal production
results.content: The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) in the Ashanti region, has shut down a second factory belonging to Unni Associates Company Limited, manufacturers of Arcan Bitters, after the company allegedly resumed production despite an earlier closure order.

results.title: Residents, school authorities demand footbridge at Aboabo after van killed 4 pupils
results.content: The death of four schoolchildren at Aboabo in the Asokore Mampong Municipality has reignited urgent calls for the construction of a footbridge on the dual carriage road that has become notorious for fatal accidents.

results.title: Tourist in South America died from peanut allergy

results.title: Made-in-Ghana products take centre stage at iNTTA exhibition in Cape Coast
results.content: Made-in-Ghana products spanning clothing, cosmetics, food, arts and crafts, herbal medicine and other locally manufactured goods took centre stage at an exhibition organised as part of the sixth Inter Tourism Expo Accra (iNTTA) in Cape Coast.

results.title: Australian MP loses both legs after alleged car attack, husband says
results.content: Helen Haines, the Australian MP who was hit by a car in what authorities say was a deliberate attack, has lost both her legs, her husband has confirmed.

results.title: Dakoa Newman calls for accountability, support for Obuasi SHTS abuse victims

results.title: PAC Chair Abena Osei-Asare praises NPA CEO, urges SOEs to address audit findings
results.content: The Chairperson of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC), Abena Osei-Asare, has urged state-owned enterprises (SOEs) to take a proactive approach to addressing operational challenges and implementing recommendations arising from audits. She made the call during a visit to the National Petroleum Authority (NPA) on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, where she commended the Authority’s Chief Executive Officer, Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, for his performance before the Committee. Ms Osei-Asare said she was impressed by Mr Tamakloe’s ability to respond to questions about the Authority’s operations and audit findings. “I must say that I was really impressed with your CEO when he came for the Public Accounts Committee. Where it's good, I'll gladly commend you, and when it's bad too, I won't mince words,” she said.

results.title: CPS pledges deeper collaboration with The Multimedia Group
results.content: The Centre for Policy Scrutiny (CPS), a Ghanaian-based research and policy advocacy think tank, has commended The Multimedia Group for supporting the dissemination of the Centre’s research findings and policy recommendations.

results.title: Gender Ministry supports 625 flood-affected residents in Hohoe with emergency cash
results.content: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP) has provided emergency cash assistance to 625 people affected by flooding in Hohoe in the Volta Region to help them meet their immediate needs and recover from the disaster.

results.title: Seven missing fishermen make contact after a week adrift at sea
results.content: Seven fishermen missing at sea for more than a week have reportedly made contact by phone, saying their canoe, Second Chance, is stranded far offshore after an engine failure.

results.title: Sam George praises GoldBod for compliance with government IT procurement rules
results.content: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovation, Samuel Nartey George, has commended the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) for what he described as its exemplary compliance with government information technology (IT) procurement regulations.

results.title: NPA seeks complete overhaul of Petroleum Authority Act 691 to address sector challenges
results.content: The National Petroleum Authority (NPA) is calling for a complete overhaul of its governing law, saying the 20-year-old legislation no longer adequately addresses the evolving challenges in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector. The Authority’s Chief Executive Officer, Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, made the call during an engagement with Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. He said the current NPA Act, 2005 (Act 691), needs to be revised to reflect changes in the petroleum market and strengthen the regulatory framework. “The National Petroleum Authority Act, Act 691, within Sections 62 to 65, governs the entire thing. Madam, I'm sure pretty soon something will be coming before Parliament. The Authority Act 691 is 20 years old. And oftentimes for a regulator, the market is always ahead of regulation,” he said.

results.title: Court halts Common Registration Examination for 792 newly trained doctors
results.content: The Human Rights Court 2 of the High Court in Accra has temporarily barred the Medical and Dental Council (MDC) from requiring 792 newly trained medical doctors to sit the Stage 1 Common Registration Examination (CRE) before obtaining provisional registration. The injunction also applies to the Attorney-General and the Ministry of Health, preventing them from enforcing the examination requirement until the court hears the substantive case and an application for an injunction on notice. The legal action was brought by the Federation of Ghana Medical Students’ Associations (FGMSA) and the affected students.

results.title: Mahama to appeal to Putin for ceasefire at Russia-Africa Summit
results.content: President John Mahama says he will appeal to Russian President Vladimir Putin to agree to a ceasefire when he travels to Russia for the Russia-Africa Summit next week. Speaking at the Financial Times Africa Summit in London, President Mahama said he intended to use the visit to urge the Russian leader to halt hostilities. “Indeed, I'm going to Russia for the Russia-Africa summit and try to convince President Putin to have a ceasefire if I can,” he said. The President also defended Ghana’s investment partnerships with countries across the world, dismissing suggestions that competition among global powers should dictate where the country seeks investment.

results.title: Ghanaian jailed in US for using relative’s identity to secure job
results.content: A 29-year-old Ghanaian, Linford Atakora, has been sentenced to approximately nine months in federal custody in the United States for fraudulently using the identity of a relative who is an American citizen to obtain employment at a home health agency.

results.title: Websites taken offline across UK & Europe as ‘critical’ security flaw hits dozens of government sites
results.content: Edinburgh and Oxford Council as well as the online home for The Traitors were taken down as was The Met Police website. According to internet monitoring website Down Detector online gaming platform Steam, Google Drive and Wordpress were all down alongside a raft of local authority websites. Error messages were displayed on the Bristol, Lambeth and Barnet council websites. Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities. It comes after the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) urged UK organisations to prepare for emergency updates to software used to run websites around the world, amid fears hackers could exploit the weaknesses to break into their systems.

results.title: Dr Zanetor urges human oversight of AI in journalism, music industry

results.title: Imperial Global Ghana, UK High Commission lead drive for science Journalism in Ghana
results.content: Thirty Ghanaian journalists have received training in emerging technologies under the UK Media Excellence for Emerging Technologies Fellowship, an initiative by Imperial Global and the British High Commission in Ghana to strengthen science journalism. The programme, now in its fourth year, forms part of the UK-Ghana Science, Technology and Innovation (ST&I) Strategy, which seeks to deepen cooperation between the two countries and improve public understanding of scientific developments. The training equipped participants with practical skills and knowledge in artificial intelligence (AI), climate change, digital tools and other emerging technologies.

results.title: YEA plans four new employment programmes for 2027 – Basintale
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) is planning four new employment programmes for 2027 as it seeks to expand opportunities for young Ghanaians in domestic services, delivery, corporate services and agriculture.

results.title: December in Ghana must deliver economic benefits beyond entertainment – Tourism Minister
results.content: The Minister for Tourism, Arts and Culture, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, has called for the annual December in Ghana festivities to deliver tangible economic benefits for Ghanaians beyond entertainment. Speaking at the launch of December in Ghana 2026 on October 20, she said the celebrations must create jobs, support local businesses and provide sustainable livelihoods for people working in the tourism and creative industries. “The true value of December in Ghana must be measured not only by the excitement of the events or the number of visitors it attracts, but also by the sustainable economic opportunities it creates for Ghanaians,” she said.

results.title: Mamprugu Traditional Council sues Jamong royals over rival chief’s enskinment in Bunkpurugu
results.content: The Overlord of the Mamprugu Traditional Area, Naa Bohagu Abdulai Mahami Sheriga, has filed an application at the High Court in Nalerigu seeking to have four people committed for contempt of court over the enskinment of a rival chief for Bunkpurugu in the North East Region.
